question: Should the exact merge head be canaried and then rolled out with the new fail-closed repair mutation authorization contract, or should this draft remain paused for a staged rollout plan?
rationale: The code review supports the implementation, but choosing when to activate stricter authorization and credential gates across live apply, merge, close, and publication automation requires ownership of the resulting security and availability tradeoff.

options.title: Canary exact head, then merge
options.body: Reconcile the final SHA, observe one stale-state rejection and one valid mutation on that exact head, then merge if receipts and deferred publication behave as designed.

options.title: Pause for staged rollout
options.body: Keep the draft open until maintainers define a narrower canary or rollback plan for the stricter fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Accept test-only rollout risk
options.body: Merge based on the extensive regression suite and hosted checks while explicitly accepting that production timing and credential failures remain unobserved.

recommendation.title: Canary exact head, then merge
recommendation.body: Reconcile the final SHA, observe one stale-state rejection and one valid mutation on that exact head, then merge if receipts and deferred publication behave as designed.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns both the merged review-activity foundation and the current mutation-boundary implementation, making them the strongest available owner for exact-head reconciliation and rollout evidence.
